title: Normalized lisse quotient filtration for continuous algebraic-closure module sheaves
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] with its extended $\ell$-adic norm topology, and the commutative condensed ring $\Lambda(P)=C(P,\Omega)$ of all continuous functions on profinite sets [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. There is no finite-subextension restriction. On each scheme $T$ put $R_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and use internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. An $R_T$-module is lisse if on a pro-etale cover it is a finite direct sum $R_T^r$, with $r=0$ allowed [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. A finite constant local model means a pro-etale local isomorphism $R_T\otimes_{\underline{\Lambda(*)}}\underline V$, with $V$ a finitely presented scalar $\Lambda(*)$-module and underlines denoting discrete constant sheaves. Constructible means having these models on a finite constructible locally closed scheme stratification [sk-def-sfb-constructible, def-constructible-stratification, def-weil-constructible-subset]. Let $M$ be a constructible $R_X$-module. There are $r\geq0$, open subschemes $\varnothing=V_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq V_r=X$ with inclusions $v_k:V_k\hookrightarrow X$, and reduced closed subschemes [def-pc-reduced-scheme] $t_k:S_k\hookrightarrow V_k$ with underlying sets $V_k\setminus V_{k-1}$. Put $L_k=t_k^*(M|_{V_k})$, using exact module inverse image [def-sfb-module-upper-star]. These modules are lisse. There are monomorphisms $M_k=v_{k!}v_k^*M\hookrightarrow M$ induced by the counits, and $0=M_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq M_r=M$, with $Q_k=M_k/M_{k-1}$ canonically isomorphic to $v_{k!}(t_k)_*L_k$. Every $a_k=v_k\circ t_k$ is a quasi-compact constructible locally closed immersion. It admits a factorization $a_k=i_k\circ j_k$ with $j_k:S_k\hookrightarrow Z_k$ open and $i_k:Z_k\hookrightarrow X$ closed [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. For every such factorization there is a canonical isomorphism $Q_k\cong(i_k)_*(j_k)_!L_k$, normalized to the identity after restriction to $S_k$, with the inverse-image coefficient rings identified with $R_T$ [def-sfb-module-lower-star, def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. All the open immersions occurring here are quasi-compact. In the ordinary unbounded derived category [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] the short exact sequence $0\to M_{k-1}\to M_k\to Q_k\to0$ gives a distinguished triangle $M_{k-1}[0]\to M_k[0]\to((i_k)_*(j_k)_!L_k)[0]\to M_{k-1}[1]$. Consequently $M[0]$ admits a construction from zero and these $r$ degree-zero stratum extensions using $r$ distinguished-triangle extensions and isomorphisms, in the inherited triangulated structure [def-weil-triangulated-category]. For $M=0$ the empty construction is allowed, including when $X=\varnothing$.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-alpha-iso] for this particular condensed ring: for every immersion $h$, $h^{-1}R_X\cong R_T$. It applies to every condensed ring, unlike a coefficient theorem limited to finite-subextension functions. The equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] identifies internal modules with modules over the corresponding section-ring sheaf, preserving underlying sheaves and actions. Thus the ringed-site module theorem [lem-pur-ringed-site-module-category-abelian] makes the ambient module category abelian. We use this identification when applying module-sheaf extension theorems below; their maps are the same maps on underlying sheaves with the transported scalar actions.

source.place: Tag 00YV, algebraic structures in a ringed topos; canonical inverse-image comparison in lem-sfb-alpha-iso.

proof.text: [lem-sfb-coefficient-heart-locally-closed-extension] gives that $X$ has Noetherian underlying space and that all its locally closed subschemes are Noetherian. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-model-stratum-filtration] to $\Lambda$ and $M$. Its constructibility hypothesis is exactly the finite constant local-model condition in the statement, not arbitrary locally finitely presented ring-sheaf modules. It supplies the finite open chain, reduced closed complements $t_k:S_k\hookrightarrow V_k$, monomorphic counits, compatible inclusions of their images, and the natural quotient maps $Q_k\cong v_{k!}(t_k)_*L_k$. In particular the counit images equal the objects $v_{k!}v_k^*M$, and the endpoints are zero and $M$. Its conclusion also supplies quasi-compactness of $v_k$ and of the open complements of $t_k$.

source.place: Tag 09Y5, lemma-noetherian-partition-refined-by-stratification; module formulation in lem-sfb-finite-model-stratum-filtration, using proetale.tex Tag 09AH.

proof.text: Evaluation on the singleton identifies $\Lambda(*)=C(*,\Omega)$ with $\Omega$ as a ring. For each local finite constant model of $L_k$, its scalar module $P$ is finitely presented over this field. The field clause of [lem-sfb-scalar-finite-free-resolutions] gives $P\cong\Omega^d$ for a finite $d\geq0$. On that same cover, scalar extension sends this basis isomorphism to $R_{S_k}\otimes_{\underline\Omega}\underline P\cong R_{S_k}^d$: the forward map sends $r\otimes(c_i)$ to $(rc_i)_i$, and its inverse sends $(r_i)_i$ to $\sum_i r_i\otimes e_i$. These inverse module maps sheafify, so this is precisely the lisse condition [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module], including rank zero.

source.place: Lisse local models; field case of the existing scalar finite-free resolution lemma.

proof.text: Each $a_k=v_kt_k$ is a locally closed immersion. The geometry clause of [lem-sfb-coefficient-heart-locally-closed-extension] makes it quasi-compact and supplies an open-then-closed factorization through its scheme-theoretic image. Its image is constructible by [def-weil-constructible-subset], being locally closed in the Noetherian space $X$. For any factorization $a_k=i_kj_k$ as in the statement, $Z_k$ is closed in $X$, hence Noetherian by the same clause, so $j_k$ is quasi-compact. Let $w_k:V_{k-1}\hookrightarrow V_k$, the open complement of $t_k$, quasi-compact by step 2. Apply [lem-sfb-locally-closed-module-extension-coherence] to $R_X$ through step 1: $\gamma_{v_k,w_k}$ identifies $M_{k-1}=v_{k-1!}v_{k-1}^*M$ with $v_{k!}w_{k!}w_k^*(M|_{V_k})$, compatibly with the counits into $M_k=v_{k!}(M|_{V_k})$. As $v_{k!}$ is exact, $Q_k\cong v_{k!}\bigl(M|_{V_k}/w_{k!}w_k^*(M|_{V_k})\bigr)$, and the localization sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] on $V_k$ (closed $t_k$, quasi-compact open $w_k$) identifies this quotient with $(t_k)_*L_k$ by its unit. We use this isomorphism $Q_k\cong v_{k!}(t_k)_*L_k$; step 2 is used only for the filtration. After $a_k^*=t_k^*v_k^*$ it is the identity of $L_k$, by $v_k^*v_{k!}\cong1$, $t_k^*(t_k)_*\cong1$ and $t_k^*w_{k!}=0$. The coherence node then gives $v_{k!}(t_k)_*\cong v_{k!}t_{k!}\cong a_{k!}\cong i_{k!}j_{k!}\cong(i_k)_*(j_k)_!$ through $\gamma_{v_k,t_k}$, $\gamma_{i_k,j_k}^{-1}$ and the closed comparisons, each restricting to the identity under the maps $r$. The composite is the required isomorphism $Q_k\cong(i_k)_*(j_k)_!L_k$, normalized to the identity after restriction to $S_k$.

source.place: Tags 09AA, 09BM, 09BN, 09AH and sites-modules.tex Tags 03DI, 03DJ; normalized factorization comparison as stated by lem-sfb-locally-closed-module-extension-coherence.

proof.text: In the abelian category from step 1, the monomorphism $M_{k-1}\hookrightarrow M_k$ and its cokernel $Q_k$ give a short exact sequence. Apply [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle] to obtain $M_{k-1}[0]\to M_k[0]\to Q_k[0]\to M_{k-1}[0][1]$ in the ordinary unbounded derived category. Insert the isomorphism of step 4 into its third vertex and into the adjacent arrows. The resulting triangle is isomorphic to the original one and hence distinguished by TR1 of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Its last object is $M_{k-1}[1]$, with the usual convention for a sheaf in degree zero.

source.place: Tag 0152, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor, applied to complexes concentrated in degree zero.

proof.text: Induct on $k=0,\ldots,r$. The starting object is $M_0[0]=0$. Given a construction of $M_{k-1}[0]$ using $k-1$ extensions, the triangle of step 5 builds $M_k[0]$ from that object and the $k$-th stratum extension using one more extension. At $k=r$ the endpoint is $M[0]$, so there are exactly $r$ such steps, with the displayed isomorphisms. If $M=0$, choose the empty construction independently of the chosen stratification; if $X$ is empty one can also take $r=0$ and $V_0=X=\varnothing$.
